info.title: OVLive API
info.description:
Realtime Dutch public-transit data. Query live vehicles or stream them over WebSocket.

**Auth**
- Data endpoints are public — no key required (this is what the official web app uses). Anonymous access is rate-limited **per client IP**, high enough that ordinary use of the map never reaches it. Supplying an API key (`Authorization: Bearer ovl_...`, `X-API-Key`, or `?key=` for the WebSocket) adds attributable **per-account** and **per-key** limits for higher sustained throughput; a `429` body names the tier that was hit. Register an account and create a key for programmatic/high-volume use.
- Account & admin endpoints use HTTP Basic (your email + password).

**WebSocket** `GET /v1/stream` (optionally `?key=ovl_...`) speaks protobuf (see packages/proto/ovlive.proto): send `Subscribe{viewport,filters}`, receive batched `Update{entered,moved,left}` diffs.

**Data sources.** Bus, tram, metro and ferry positions come from BISON KV6; **train** positions come from NS InfoPlus, a separate feed with different properties:
- Trains have `dataowner` `IFF` (the namespace gtfs-nl uses for rail), so a vehicle id looks like `IFF:8743`, where `8743` is the train number. `realtime_trip_id` is gtfs-nl's own value, e.g. `IFF:SPR:8743`, and `line` is the train type code (`SPR`, `IC`, `ICD`, `ICE`, ...).
- **`delay_seconds` is only meaningful when `delay_known` is true.** Unknown and on-time are both `0`, so a client that ignores the flag reports trains as punctual when their punctuality is simply unknown. The position feed carries no punctuality at all; it comes from a second NS feed (InfoPlus RitInfo) published per journey revision rather than continuously, so train coverage builds up over time and is never complete.
- `at_stop`/`current_stop_id` are never set for trains (the position feed has no stop passages), and their trip plan is pure schedule (shift it by the trip delay yourself, and only when `delay_known`). On a departure board a live train with no punctuality yet has `delay_seconds: null`, and `expected_departure` equal to `scheduled_departure`.
- Only NS-operated trains report positions. Other rail concessions (Arriva, Blauwnet, ...) are in the schedule but not in this feed, and a small share of NS runs (empty stock, units without GPS telemetry) appear with no matching trip: `line`, `destination` and `operator` are then empty while `vehicle_type` is still `train`.

- **RET metros carry no coordinates at all** (the KV6 records omit rd-x/rd-y or send the -1 "unknown" marker), so their position is **schedule-anchored**: the vehicle's `lat`/`lon` is the station of its last confirmed stop call, resolved by matching the message time minus punctuality against the matched GTFS trip's scheduled calls. Such vehicles have `schedule_positioned: true` and hop station-to-station rather than moving continuously; the position is never interpolated between stations. A vehicle with GPS always reports its real fix (`schedule_positioned: false`).

**Deprecated endpoints** tagged `Deprecated` reproduce the pre-Rust OVLive API exactly so existing consumers keep working during migration. They will be removed — do not build against them.

delete.summary: Delete one of your API keys

parameters.name: owners
parameters.description: comma list of dataowners, e.g. RET,HTM

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Cap on returned vehicles; omit for the full snapshot. With `search`, results are ranked before truncating (exact vehicle-number/line match first, then prefix, then any other field) so a small limit returns the most relevant matches.

200.description: `{ count, total, vehicles }` — `count` is the number returned, `total` how many matched before `limit`.

401.description: Invalid/revoked key (only when a key is supplied)

get.description:
`{ vehicle, trip_id }` — the parts of the vehicle view that change. This is the endpoint to poll.

The schedule half (route shape and stop list) is **not** here: it is constant for the duration of a trip and is served separately by `/v1/vehicles/{id}/trip`. `trip_id` is the matched GTFS trip (null when the vehicle isn't matched to one), so refetch that endpoint only when this value changes.

get.summary: Vehicle trip plan: route shape + scheduled stops (fetch once per trip)
get.description:
`{ trip_id, route_shape, stops }` — the schedule behind the vehicle's current trip. Nothing in it changes while the vehicle runs that trip, so fetch it once and refetch only when `trip_id` from `/v1/vehicles/{id}` changes. `trip_id` is null, with an empty shape and no stops, when GTFS hasn't matched the vehicle to a trip.

`route_shape` is `[[lat, lon], ...]`. `stops` covers the **whole** trip in order — `{ stop_id, name, lat, lon, stop_sequence, scheduled_arrival, scheduled_departure }`, seconds since the operating day's local midnight (may exceed 86400 for after-midnight service).

There are deliberately no expected times and no "upcoming" filtering, so that this payload stays constant: expected is `scheduled + delay_seconds` from the live vehicle (only meaningful when `delay_known`), and the stops still ahead are those from the one nearest the vehicle's position onward — that stop itself when it reports `at_stop`, otherwise the next one once its `scheduled_departure + delay_seconds` has passed.

get.summary: Live public line numbers with counts

get.description: **Deprecated — will be removed.** Byte-compatible shim for consumers of the pre-Rust OVLive API: camelCase keys, capitalised enums (`"Bus"`, `"OnStop"`), `yyyyMMdd` `operatingDay`, and plain-text (not JSON) error bodies. Responses carry `Deprecation: true`. Returns `{trips:[{id,agency,transportType,vehicleNumber,lat,lon,line,timestamp}]}`. Capped by `MAX_SPATIAL_RESULTS` (default 1500). Use `GET /v1/vehicles?bbox=` instead.

parameters.description: Comma-separated extra trip ids, included regardless of the viewport

400.description: `invalid neLat` / `invalid viewport bounds` / `viewport too large` (plain text). Area is capped by `MAX_VIEWPORT_AREA`, default 2.0 deg².

401.description: Invalid/revoked key (only when a key is supplied)

get.summary: Scheduled times for every stop of a trip
get.description: **Deprecated — will be removed.** Byte-compatible shim for consumers of the pre-Rust OVLive API: camelCase keys, capitalised enums (`"Bus"`, `"OnStop"`), `yyyyMMdd` `operatingDay`, and plain-text (not JSON) error bodies. Responses carry `Deprecation: true`. Returns `{id,active,line,headsign,transportType,punctuality,state,operatingDay,stops:[{stopName,userStopCode,stopSequence,scheduledArrival,scheduledDeparture}]}`. **Two known differences:** `realtimeArrival`/`realtimeDeparture` are always absent (they required per-stop realtime passages, which cannot be joined to gtfs-nl — see CLAUDE.md), and ended trips 404 because no trip history is persisted, so `active` is always `true`. Both fields were `omitempty`, so the shape is unchanged. No replacement yet.

tags.name: Deprecated
tags.description: Byte-compatible shim for consumers of the pre-Rust OVLive API. **Temporary — these will be removed once those consumers have migrated.** They intentionally keep the old paths, camelCase keys, capitalised enum values and plain-text error bodies, so they do not match the conventions of the rest of this API. Every response carries `Deprecation: true` and a `Link: </docs>; rel="deprecation"` header. Prefer `/v1/vehicles*`; the stops endpoints have no replacement yet.
